headline: Witkoff calls Putin 'a humanitarian' at start of St. Petersburg meeting
dek: Witkoff told Putin: 'You talk so much about my president, President Trump, being a humanitarian. You are a humanitarian also, sir, and I salute that, I commend you, and I thank you again' — tied to the Hubbard release (Trump: no swap needed; Peskov: freed out of 'humanitarian considerations').
sources: Steve Witkoff, US Special Envoy (televised opening remarks to Vladimir Putin, Constantine Palace)
fault_line: Pragmatic diplomacy to close a deal — or capitulation to a war criminal while the bombs still fall?

sections.what_happened: Witkoff told Putin: 'You talk so much about my president, President Trump, being a humanitarian. You are a humanitarian also, sir, and I salute that, I commend you, and I thank you again' — tied to the Hubbard release (Trump: no swap needed; Peskov: freed out of 'humanitarian considerations'). GOP Sens. Thom Tillis ('WTF, Steve? ... embarrassing and outrageous') and John Cornyn ('Putin is stone cold killer') rebuked him on X. As Witkoff spoke, Russian strikes on Ukrainian cities continued, killing at least four (The Times). NY Post notes Monday's Nova Vodolaha park drone strike killed six incl. teacher Inna Mariukhna and her 14-month-old daughter Anhelina; UN: 328 civilians killed in September. Trump's Oct 19 line via Kyiv Independent: 'Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine. They haven't been doing much.'
sections.what_verified: The Times (updated <1h, crawled <1h), NY Post (updated 1h), The Print, UNN (citing Politico), Kyiv Independent YouTube segment, Gerashchenko clip of Russian state media video. Cross-partisan + international pickup; quote text identical across outlets.
sections.what_disputed: Diplomatic-flattery defense: remark tied specifically to Hubbard release ('Because of you he is going home to his family'); Putin released a wrongfully-detained American at no cost; no new policy concession made. Ushakov separately said Ukraine/EU approaches lacked 'substance' — substance talks unaffected by the optics.
sections.why_matters: Washington's own envoy bows to Moscow with 'humanitarian' praise even as Russian strikes kill civilians the same day — and the hawks on his own side erupt. The outrage is real; so is the flattery's purpose. Play the quote verbatim, show both, ask the fault-line question.
sections.context: Background: US/Russia — NEW in window: Witkoff calls Putin 'a humanitarian' at start of St. Petersburg meeting; Republican senators publicly rebuke him
